paper.title_en: Emergent $\mathrm{SU}(2)_2$ Wess-Zumino-Witten criticality in an anisotropic spin-1 Kitaev-$Γ$ chain
paper.abstract_en: Bond-directional interactions underpin unconventional quantum phenomena, yet their interplay with single-ion anisotropy remains elusive. Here we combine large-scale density-matrix renormalization group calculations and bosonization to investigate the spin-1 Kitaev-$Γ$ chain. Positive anisotropy drives a smooth crossover from the Kitaev regime to the trivial large-$D$ limit, contrasting with the topological Haldane-to-large-$D$ transition in the spin-1 Heisenberg chain. This adiabatic evolution reshapes the excitation spectrum, nonlocal correlations, and thermodynamic signatures. Conversely, negative anisotropy induces a changeover from a first-order to a continuous dimer-Haldane transition. The continuous transition exhibits $\mathrm(2)_2$ Wess-Zumino-Witten criticality with central charge of $3/2$, despite the absence of microscopic continuous symmetry. Bosonization predicts a spin-correlation exponent $η= 3/4$, consistent with our numerical estimate of $0.77(3)$. Our findings reveal how bond-directional interactions shape distinctive gapped regimes and emergent conformal criticality.
